issues.claim: The clerk's scratch commit resubmits filtered lists that §11.2 compares unfiltered. VAT-R1-03's fix makes V10 §3.5 step 3 (l.1450–1457) read the item from `preview(scratch, events, { filtered: true })`, then commit by `edit(scratch, events, { filtered: true })` 'with the preview's fates and renames filled, §11.2's resubmission form'. It adds: 'A commit that answers otherwise than its preview (a `conflict`, or a `confirm` whose fates differ) refuses the item with that answer and records the preview equality check's defect'. But the preview's lists are the filtered ones: §11.2 *`filtered`* renders fates and renames under the caller's key (a withheld place by address and kind, a concealed use and an unexcavated element absent). §11.2 *Confirming fates* commits a resubmission only 'when a fresh dry run computes the same fates and renames', and *Knowledge* states that a `confirm` result goes only to an editing role, unfiltered. So whenever the session's effective key withholds an entry of an item's fates or renames — under View as, or with a host-lowered editor key (V10 §2.3) — the engine answers `confirm`. The scratch cannot have moved between the two calls, so the difference is the filter's. Yet V10 refuses a lawful item and writes a `previewMismatch` defect. Round 1's text confirmed a scratch `confirm` at once, and V10 §4.2 (1) avoids the trap on the user's document by previewing unfiltered and comparing the filtered projection; step 3 no longer shares that rule.
issues.required_change: V10 §3.5 step 3, after '§11.2's resubmission form, as V10 §4.2 (1) commits:', reads: 'a `confirm` answer — which a filtered resubmission receives wherever the session's key withholds an entry of the fates or renames (§11.2 *`filtered`*, *Confirming fates*) — is confirmed on the scratch at once, `confirm(scratch, token, fates, renames)` with that answer's own lists. A `confirm` result reaches an editing client unfiltered (§11.2 *Knowledge*), and the scratch is disposable. This holds whenever the filtered projection of the answer's lists at the session's effective key equals the preview's, compared as V10 §4.2 (1) compares (counts, fates by address, renames). Only a `conflict`, or a `confirm` whose projection differs, refuses the item with that answer and records the preview equality check's defect (V10 §2.8)'. T-V10-11's scratch clause adds a View as fixture whose declaration moves a concealed use and renames a withheld place: the item commits on the scratch and records no defect. J-V10.127 adds 'a filtered resubmission's `confirm` is confirmed with its own lists'.

issues.claim: V09 §4.21.13 (1) (l.3616–3617) states item 123's one comparison as 'an element shows damaged when the level is at or above its threshold' ('R2-38's one comparison'). Its home, §6.3 *Plan damage*, says 'the element shows damaged exactly while the level is above 0 and at least t — a level of 0 damages nothing, so a building never decayed draws its plan unchanged (`item123.damage`)'; V03 §5.6 (2) (a) and V11 §3.25.10 say the same. V11's ranges admit lo = 0 and u = 0 (VDC2-07), so V09's reading shows a damage line on a never-decayed building. That contradicts V09's own (4) ('A building never decayed shows no line') and T-V9-86's no-op clause, and the panel and the plan disagree on the same building. The model and rendering forms of this slip are VDC2-07 and VRC2T-13; V09's is unraised.
issues.required_change: V09 §4.21.13 (1): 'by R2-38's one comparison — an element shows damaged when the level is at or above its threshold —' → 'by §6.3's one comparison — an element shows damaged while the level is above 0 and at least its threshold, so a level of 0 shows nothing —'.

issues.claim: V10 §3.9a's damage part (l.1803–1808) restates the comparison as 'each plan element shown damaged once the building's decay level … reaches the element's one keyed threshold (§6.3's `plan.damage`, …), the one comparison every reader makes'. 'Reaches' without §6.3's 'above 0' reads as level ≥ t. With V11's lo = 0 that damages an element at level 0, which V10's own *Absent* bullet ('a building never decayed has none … `item123.damage`') and T-V10-53's no-op clause exclude. The text holds two readings of one rule, and it restates a rule whose home is §6.3.
issues.required_change: V10 §3.9a: 'reaches the element's one keyed threshold (§6.3's `plan.damage`, within its element kind's range of V11's rows), the one comparison every reader makes' → 'is above 0 and at least the element's one keyed threshold — §6.3's comparison (`plan.damage`, within its element kind's range of V11's rows), the one every reader makes, so a level of 0 damages nothing'.

issues.claim: The host's 'layers shown' command writes a field the set writes only by a logged event. §11.3 *The host's view commands* (l.16282–16285, new this round for item 125 (c)) has a host drive 'the layers shown (`view.set` of the view's layer choices, §8.4's `LayerSpec.visible`)'. Elsewhere `LayerSpec` is the document's style state, written by the logged `setLayer`: §7.1's binding (T12 `dress`); §7.4's row (l.11019: 'setLayer … style state (canonical, outside the model digest) | log | … | inverse'); II.7 (l.20565: the underground toggle 'sets the underground `LayerSpec.visible` through `setLayer`'); V09 §4.3 and l.4050 ('the style's layer spec (`setLayer`, logged)', J-V9.54); V10 §4.1's T12 `layer` → `setLayer { layer, spec: { visible } }`. `view.set` patches only the view keys that travel (§11.3, l.16195), and `LayerSpec` is no view key. So a host's toggle changes neither the log nor the style state, while the same toggle by a user or the clerk is a logged, undoable event that travels as `doc.changed`: one command, two meanings, and a reload or another client shows different layers. §7.7 item 1 (l.11687) and V08 (`setView`'s comment l.489; §3.16 (4), (6) (g)) restate the three commands as `view.set`, and V09 §4.2 (l.1654) calls the visibility a layer switch sets 'view state only'.
issues.required_change: One path for a layer's visibility, the one §7.1, §7.4 and §8.4 give. (1) §11.3 *The host's view commands*: 'the layers shown (`view.set` of the view's layer choices, §8.4's `LayerSpec.visible`)' → 'the layers shown (a `setLayer { layer, spec: { visible } }` sent by `doc.apply`, as a user's layer toggle is that logged event — §7.1's binding, T12 `dress`; §7.4's `setLayer` row; `LayerSpec` is the document's style state, §8.4, and no view key, so `view.set` never carries it)'. The week (`view.set { week }`) and the selection (`view.set { select }`) stay `view.set` commands, keeping R2-33 (b)'s three commands. (2) The restatements follow the same form: §7.7 item 1, V08's `setView` comment and its §3.16 (4) and (6) (g). (3) V09 §4.2's '(§7.8's layer controls, view state only)' reads '(§7.8's layer controls: `LayerSpec.visible`, written by `setLayer`, §8.4)'.

issues.claim: Two lists derived for the view — DR44's standing crisis looks and DR43's festival list — are read by three members, and no member produces them through an interface. `live.crises` evaluates DR44 in the generation worker over the model, the view state and the key (§8.2 *The layer*, l.12931). V09's Show crises controls, crisis card, why lines and Find's `crises` section read 'the legend's crisis entries (§9.5: the values drawn) … one evaluation' (V09 §4.21.12 (3), l.3571–3572; §2.12 l.1005: the card 'derived from the standing overlays by DR44 at `effectiveKey()`'). V10's `read_map { kind: 'look' }` takes `LookAnswer.crises` 'by §9.5's legend entries' (V10 §3.5 l.1441; §1.2 l.185), needing each look's condition id, map row, severity, weeks and a disaster's districts (V10 §2.13 l.1001–1011). But §9.5's legend is a drawn furniture panel (a glyph, a name and weeks) that no data structure holds, and §11.2 has no query kind, answer type or event returning the standing looks. The main thread does not hold the model, §10.2's crisis table, V01's `disasterDistricts` or V06's `frontierFor`, so neither reader can run DR44 itself. The festival list is the same: V09 §4.21.8 (1) and V10's `LookAnswer.festivals` read 'DR43 … from the dossier', with no read on the API. These are dangling inputs (principle (7)). V10's hand-off CVR-V10-22 asked V09 to expose the evaluation; V09 cites only the legend. VV910-r2-04 covers only V09's missing citation of V01's districts.
issues.required_change: §11.2 adds one view-bound reader kind, `{ kind: 'looks'; view: ViewHandle }`, answered as `LooksAnswer { week: number /* §2.9's week */; yearWeek: number; festivals: { id: string; name?: string; weeks: [number, number]; shown: boolean }[] /* DR43's list in window order */; crises: { look: CrisisLookKind; condition?: Id; source?: { from: 'stressor'|'archetype'|'event'; key: string }; sinceWeek?: number; untilWeek?: number; severity: number; forces?: { headcount: number; groups: number }; districts?: Id[]; massed?: true }[] /* DR44's standing looks, or the preview, in the legend's order */ }`. It is computed in the generation worker by the same evaluation `live.crises` draws and §9.5's legend lists, admitted at the view's effective key by *Knowledge* (a withheld condition absent and uncounted); its call-table row reads 'out: one answer, ≤ 64 KB'. The readers cite it in place of 'the legend's entries': V09 §4.21.8 (1), §4.21.12 (3)–(7) and §2.12's crisis-card row; V10 §2.13 (`LookAnswer.festivals` and `.crises` as projections of `LooksAnswer`) and §3.5's `look` read; V10 §1.2's §9.5 row becomes a §11.2 row.
